title: Bayesian Modelling Framework for Evaluating Energy Development Impacts on Sage-Grouse
author: Prochazka, O'Neil, et al.
materials: During this step we developed a population matrix model within a Bayesian framework that identified energy development impacts on specific vital rates using a two-stage (control-impact) modeling process. The first stage of the two-stage process involved modeling background sources of variation attributed to environmental conditions (referred to as ‘confounder covariates’) for each demographic rate using data collected from study sites that were not associated with energy development projects. This step was done to estimate environmental effects (i.e., parameters) in the absence of energy development, and ultimately formed a baseline prediction (at every MCMC iteration) for each animal location within energy development sites, given local environmental conditions (i.e., locally recorded data). During stage 2, a second likelihood, run concurrently (concurrent to confounder likelihood) and within the same JAGS wrapper function, was used to estimate energy development-related covariates in the presence of confounder predictions (i.e., the product of control-informed parameter(s) and locally recorded data). We performed these two stages for each vital rate model, thereby alleviating issues of spatial autocorrelation among confounder and geothermal covariates. Furthermore, the method accounts for the full uncertainty in confounder effects by estimating a new baseline likelihood at every iteration of the model.

steps.title: Collect Lek Count Data
steps.instruction: Conduct annual lek surveys for male sage-grouse to serve as an abundance index.

substeps.instruction: Perform 3–4 10-minute surveys per lek site during the breeding period (March–May) to overlap peak attendance.
Conduct counts between 30 minutes before and 90 minutes after sunrise using binoculars or spotting scopes.
Record counts from all known leks (n=103) within 60 km of geothermal infrastructure.
Perform surveys over a 14-year period (2005–2018), divided into 7 years before (2005–2011) and 7 years after (2012–2018) the onset of geothermal operations.
Apply QA/QC procedures and retain maximum annual counts for analysis.

steps.title: Analyze Population Patterns (Analysis 1)
steps.instruction: Use a Before-After Control-Impact (BACI) framework to assess changes in population growth rates and extirpation probabilities.

substeps.instruction: Calculate Euclidean distance between population nodes (leks) and the nearest point or edge of infrastructure.
Assign nodes to 'impact' or 'control' groups based on six candidate distance thresholds: 2 km, 5 km, 10 km, 15 km, 20 km, and 30 km.
Define the control group as leks at distances greater than the selected threshold up to 57.2 km.
Verify SSM assumptions of interannual constancy for observation errors prior to modeling.
For lek absence rates, subset data to the final two years of before (2011–2012) and after (2017–2018) periods.

steps.title: Monitor Individual Demographic Performance
steps.instruction: Track individual female sage-grouse using telemetry to investigate survival and reproduction.

substeps.instruction: Capture female sage-grouse (n=1,049) using standard spotlighting techniques during spring and late summer/fall.
Outfit birds with necklace-style VHF radio-transmitters (Advanced Telemetry Systems) with mortality signals pulsing after ≥8 h of inactivity.
Determine age (yearling: >1 and <2 years; adult: ≥2 years) by examining wing feather characteristics.
Relocate birds twice per week during reproductive season (March–September) and once per month during fall/winter via fixed-wing aircraft, circling from 30–50 m.

steps.title: Monitor Nest and Brood Success
steps.instruction: Track nesting and brood-rearing progress to determine vital rates.

substeps.instruction: Confirm nests when females are found in the same position on two consecutive relocations; visually confirm with binoculars at ~10 m distance.
Record clutch size opportunistically during nest recesses or incidental flushing.
Monitor nests at least twice weekly until fate is determined (success: ≥1 egg hatched; failure: depredation or abandonment).
For failed nests, monitor twice weekly to confirm renest locations.
Count chicks every 10 days until the brood reaches 50 days post-hatch; if no chicks are detected, conduct a follow-up survey within 24–48 h.
Exclude data if relocation dates are missing, status of nest/chicks/adults is missing, or unique identification is impossible.

steps.title: Quantify Environmental and Infrastructure Covariates
steps.instruction: Extract land cover and distance data to account for environmental effects on demographic rates.

substeps.instruction: Extract 30 m² land cover data (National Land Cover Database) for: herbaceous perennial vegetation, little/big sagebrush, total shrub canopy, annual grass, and sagebrush height.
Extract tree canopy cover from high-resolution mapping and riparian/wet meadow areas from LANDFIRE products (30 m² resolution).
Calculate percent cover within radii of 167.9 m (8.7 ha), 439.5 m (61.5 ha), and 1451.7 m (661.4 ha) using ArcMap 10.5.
For nesting periods, include 30-m and 75-m extents.
Calculate Euclidean and exponential decay distances to perennial/intermittent streams and springs using National Hydrography Dataset.
Calculate topographic roughness of the terrain.

Digitize geothermal infrastructure using high-resolution aerial imagery to calculate Euclidean distances from nest/brood/adult locations to the nearest edge of the plant (DGP) and the nearest edge of the footprint (DGF).

steps.title: Develop Topographic Impedance Surface (TIS)
steps.instruction: Create a continuous covariate index to approximate the dispersion of noise and light from geothermal infrastructure.

substeps.instruction: Create a minimum convex polygon (MCP) based on all telemetry locations.
Create Euclidean spatial lines connecting every 30 m² grid cell within the MCP to the center cell of the geothermal power plant.
Extract elevation values for every cell intersected by the spatial lines using a 30-m resolution Digital Elevation Model (DEM).
Subtract these values from a baseline elevation derived between start and end points using a constant slope.
Assign the maximum difference along each Euclidean line to the start cell to create the TIS.

steps.title: Calculate Raven Density Index (RDI)
steps.instruction: Estimate relative raven densities at nest sites using hierarchical distance sampling.

substeps.instruction: Conduct raptor-raven point count surveys from mid-March to mid-September (2012–2018) within MCPs, performing ≥200 surveys per field site per year.
Record time, distance, and bearing of all observed ravens using binoculars, digital rangefinder, GPS, and compass.
Employ a detection function g[r,z] using a half-normal key function in R 4.0 ('unmarked' package), with viewshed and percent forested landscape as covariates.
Assign observations to 5 distance classes: 225, 450, 675, 900, and 1,125 m.
Use a Horvitz-Thompson-like estimator to calculate RDI for each nest location using raven count data within a 3.5 km radius.

steps.title: Implement Bayesian Population Process Modeling
steps.instruction: Apply a two-stage Bayesian population matrix model to identify impacts on vital rates.

substeps.instruction: Stage 1: Model background variation (confounder covariates) using data from sites without energy development to estimate environmental effects and form a baseline prediction.
Stage 2: Run a second likelihood concurrently within a JAGS wrapper function to estimate energy development-related covariates in the presence of confounder predictions.
For the nest survival model, incorporate RDI and investigate a three-way interaction between DGI, TIS, and RDI (including all two-way interactions).
